actions.reason: No candidate submitted. In the concurrent benchmark, most of the instruction count goes to FNV-hashing each item once per key. That covers 27 keys over 64-byte items for the big filter, and 3 to 5 keys over 32-byte items for the 24 small filters. The FnvHasher byte loop already appears to be near the floor of three instructions per byte. Earlier measured attempts made every metric worse: hand-unrolling it, word-at-a-time loops, hashing several keys in one pass, and forcing #[inline]. Replacing checked_rem with a plain `%` changed concurrent_ir by about 0.03%. Loading the word before fetch_or made concurrent_ir worse, and fetch_or followed by a single-bit test likely already compiles to `lock bts`. The work outside hashing is small next to the hashing cost, by rough estimate rather than measurement: the Bloom/ConcurrentBloom conversions, the count_ones pass and clear(). I don't expect a behaviour-preserving change in bloom/src to reach the 1% minimum on concurrent_ir, so I'm not spending an evaluation on a guess.

journal.text:
I read bloom/src/bloom.rs and the bench in bloom/examples/lineage_bench.rs. I searched for the concurrent paths and for the BitVec conversion, truncate and into_boxed_slice functions, looking for overhead outside hashing. I made no edits and ran no sandbox evaluations.

Nothing was measured this session. Most of the instruction count in the concurrent benchmark is FNV hashing, done once per key per item. The big filter uses 27 keys over 64-byte items. The 24 small filters use 3 to 5 keys over 32-byte items. The FnvHasher byte loop looks close to its floor of three instructions per byte. Earlier measured attempts made every metric worse. I submitted no candidate.

I now think the cost here is the number of hash passes, not the code that performs each pass. Making each pass a little faster will not move the totals.

Next time, try computing one hash per item and deriving all the keys from it. That would have to be checked to see whether bloom.rs semantics allow the bit positions to change.
